comments.body:
🚨 severity: BLOCKING —
🚨 **BLOCKING: red CI (`crap` check) — 25 new unit-test failures, all from one eager `file_write` global reference**

CI on `21d06ac7` fails with `9651 passed, 25 failed`. Measured locally against this branch and against `origin/main`:

- `origin/main`: 10451 passed, **3 failed** (pre-existing set: Story Questions pattern, gh-922 dedup scratch, wiki_publisher validation)
- this branch: 10464 passed, **28 failed** → **25 new failures, all introduced by this PR** (test_preCliDevelopmentSetup.js ×19, test_workingDir.js ×3, test_developmentModePlan.js ×1 + cascades in the gh-716/gh-1042/gh-1364 suites)

Every new failure carries the same signature: `Plan-mode setup failed: ReferenceError: file_write is not defined`.

**Root cause** — `materializePlanAppendix` resolves the dmtools global **eagerly, before the mode gate**:

```javascript
function materializePlanAppendix(customParams, io) {
    var write = (io && io.file_write) || file_write;   // ← line 211: evaluated even when mode ≠ plan
    var resolved = readAppendixText(customParams, io);
    if (!resolved.active) { ... }                       // ← the zero-IO early-out happens too late
```

In production dmtools GralJS `file_write` is a defined global, so real legs don't crash — but in the Node test harness (`js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js`, which the CI `crap` check runs) `file_write` does not exist, so **every** `preCliDevelopmentSetup.action()` invocation now throws, the new wrapper (`runPlanModeAppendixStepOrReport`) catches it, posts a setup-error comment and fails the leg. That is why 19 previously-green tests (base passes `test_preCliDevelopmentSetup.js` 100/0 — verified) go red, including suites unrelated to plan mode. The PR description's verification claim ("no new failures vs base — 15 pre-existing, identical set") is factually wrong on both numbers.

**Fix** (mirrors the `readAppendixText` structure — note its `var read = ... || file_read;` on line 172 is the same eager pattern, currently masked only because the harness defines `file_read`; fix both in one pass):

```javascript
function materializePlanAppendix(customParams, io) {
    var resolved = readAppendixText(customParams, io);
    if (!resolved.active) {
        return { ok: false, active: false, ... };
    }
    var write = (io && io.file_write) || file_write;   // resolved only on active plan legs
    ...
```

This also restores the module's own P1 spirit: an inactive leg should not *touch* the IO surface at all, only skip it.
